newsitem.title: UK: London coffee now up 40 percent since early January.
newsitem.headline: London coffee now up 40 percent since early January.

text.p: London coffee futures extended a rally on Tuesday to stand some 40 percent higher than a month ago at $1,680 a tonne on fears that a strike in Colombia may put a new squeeze on already-tight supplies.
The benchmark May contract for Robusta coffee traded on the London Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) soared $80 a tonne at the opening before profit-taking trimmed gains slightly.
The new advance was inspired by a rally in New York on Monday where the higher quality Arabica coffee ended at a 20-month high on the March contract at 158.65 cents per pound.
The Colombian strike by some 800,000 state workers, due to start by midnight on Monday, puts yet another dampener on coffee supplies already pressured by expected low crops in Brazil, traders said.
"The weight of the money is on the buy side, you can't roll anything out of this market at the moment," said one trader. "I don't think we need to be here but that's a worthless argument."
London coffee prices have risen by about 40 percent since the January 7 when the bellwether contract was $1,203 per tonne.
Elli Gifford, technical analyst at Investment Research, said a conclusive close above $1,620 in London's robusta could trigger a move to at least $1,800 dating back from June 28.

"A continued commitment to the market could well prove worthwhile," said Gifford. But New York Arabica prices were unlikely to sustain their high pace for much longer and could see some profit taking.
